=== MODULAR CHARACTER PROMPT TEMPLATE (any humanoid NPC, any weapon) ==============

Makes a cut-out ("paper puppet") character for the game's RigPuppet system: 5 body-part
sheets (one per view) + 1 weapon-effects sheet. The game rigs the parts on a skeleton,
animates idle / walk / attack in 8 directions (it mirrors E, SE, NE to get W, SW, NW),
and fires the projectiles from the effects sheet.

Everything in {CURLY BRACES} is a placeholder: replace it before sending, and delete any
line marked (optional) that doesn't apply. Leave every other line exactly as it is - the
sprite extractor (tools/extract_sprites.py) depends on the canvas, grid and background.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HOW TO USE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 1. Fill in the CHARACTER CARD below once. Copy it unchanged into every message, so
    every sheet describes the character with exactly the same words.
 2. FIRST SHEET - FRONT 3/4. Attach the character reference image (concept art, or
    a finished parts sheet of a similar character whose layout and style you want to
    copy). Send PROMPT A with {VIEW} = the FRONT 3/4 line.
 3. Check it against the CHECKLIST at the bottom. Regenerate until it passes: every
    other sheet copies this one, so its mistakes copy too.
 4. OTHER FOUR VIEWS. Send PROMPT A 4 more times, with {VIEW} = FRONT, SIDE, BACK 3/4,
    BACK. Each time, attach the reference AND the finished FRONT 3/4 sheet, and keep
    the line "Match the attached FRONT 3/4 sheet..." in the prompt.
 5. EFFECTS. Send PROMPT B once, with the weapon's effects filled in.
 6. Save the files as:
      <faction>_npc_<id>_parts_front34.png  ..._front.png  ..._side.png
      ..._back34.png  ..._back.png           <faction>_fx_<id>.png
    and add them to RIG_SHEETS / FX_SHEETS in tools/extract_sprites.py.

THE 5 VIEW LINES (paste one as {VIEW}):
 FRONT 3/4 - turned 45 degrees toward the viewer, facing down-right (south-east); the character's right side (near) is toward the viewer.
 FRONT - facing the viewer directly (south); the character's right side is on the viewer's left.
 SIDE - full profile facing RIGHT (east); the character's right side (near) faces the viewer.
 BACK 3/4 - turned 45 degrees away from the viewer, facing up-right (north-east); we see the back and the right side.
 BACK - facing directly away from the viewer (north); the character's right side is on the viewer's right.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CHARACTER CARD (fill in once, paste into every message)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{CHARACTER}       who / what it is, in one line.
                  e.g. "a sci-fi triceratops humanoid female priest-archer"
{BODY}            build, height, skin / fur / scales, head shape, horns, ears, tail.
                  e.g. "slim, scaly olive skin, a red-and-cream spiral frill, two brown horns"
{OUTFIT}          clothes and armour, top to bottom, with colours and ornaments.
                  e.g. "cream robe with red spiral borders, gold-and-blue armour bands, sandals"
{CAPE}            the loose back cloth (cape, cloak, banner, quiver, wings, backpack) -
                  or "none".
{FRONT CLOTH}     the loose front piece that swings when walking (apron, tabard, kilt
                  panel, tassels) - or "none".
{PALETTE}         3-5 main colours, e.g. "cream, brick red, gold, deep blue, glowing cyan".
{STYLE}           e.g. "painted game art, crisp clean outlines" (keep it the same for
                  every character in the game).
{WEAPON}          the weapon at rest, its colours and size.
                  e.g. "a gold tech longbow with glowing cyan panels, as tall as the character"
{WEAPON ACTIVE}   the weapon in use.
                  e.g. "the same bow fully drawn, string pulled back, a glowing arrow nocked"
                  / "the rifle with its muzzle glowing and vents open"
{WEAPON ALT}      a second item: sidearm, shield, staff, tool, empty-handed spell glow -
                  or the weapon from another angle. (optional: "none" leaves the cell empty)
{HANDS}           the third hand pose the weapon needs.
                  e.g. "hand pinching a bowstring" / "hand on a trigger" /
                  "hand open, palm forward, casting"
{EFFECTS}         what the weapon shoots and how it hits (for PROMPT B).
                  e.g. "cyan laser arrows, plasma arrows, a release flash, impact bursts"

==================================================================================
PROMPT A - BODY-PART SHEET (send once per view)
==================================================================================
Create a modular cut-out animation sprite sheet of this character:
{CHARACTER}. {BODY}. Wearing {OUTFIT}. Back cloth: {CAPE}. Front cloth: {FRONT CLOTH}.
Colours: {PALETTE}. Weapon: {WEAPON}.
Copy the attached reference exactly: the same design, colours, ornaments and proportions.
(For views 2-5) Match the attached FRONT 3/4 sheet: the same character, colours, scale,
part list and cell layout, only seen from a different direction.

VIEW FOR THIS WHOLE SHEET: {VIEW}

The pieces will be rigged on a skeleton and animated in a game (idle, walking, attacking
with the weapon), so every body part is drawn SEPARATELY, like a paper cut-out puppet
taken apart at its joints.

=== CANVAS (exact) ===
- Image size: exactly 2048 x 960 pixels.
- Background: one flat solid colour, pure magenta #FF00FF, everywhere that is not a piece.
  No gradient, no texture, no vignette, no shadows, no floor, no grid lines, no frames,
  no panels, no labels, no text, no arrows, no guide lines.
- Grid: 8 columns x 3 rows of invisible cells, each cell exactly 256 x 320 pixels
  (cell x = col*256, cell y = row*320). Exactly ONE piece per cell, never crossing its
  cell, at least 6 px of magenta around every piece. Pieces in one row never touch
  pieces in the next row: leave a clear magenta band between the rows.
- A long weapon must still fit inside its own cell: scale the weapon down rather than
  letting it cross into the next cell.

=== STYLE AND VIEW ===
- {STYLE}. No motion blur, no depth of field, no glow bleeding outside the piece.
- Orthographic, NO perspective. Seen from slightly above (30 degree isometric camera).
  Every piece is seen from the same view given above.
- Light from the upper-left on every piece. Even lighting, no cast shadows.

=== SCALE (important) ===
- Every piece is drawn at EXACTLY the same scale as the assembled figure in row 0, cell 0.
  Put back together, the pieces rebuild that figure exactly.
- Head, hands and feet are NOT enlarged, and limbs are NOT shortened to fit their
  cells: the proportions stay realistic.
- The head is in proportion to the body (about 1/6 to 1/7 of the standing height for a
  human build); the neck is short.

=== REST POSE (every body piece is drawn in it) ===
Standing straight, feet slightly apart, arms hanging straight down a little away from the
body, palms in, nothing in the hands, mouth closed, eyes open, looking forward, cape and
cloth hanging straight down.

=== NEAR AND FAR ===
NEAR = the character's own RIGHT arm and leg. FAR = the LEFT arm and leg.
- In FRONT 3/4, SIDE and BACK 3/4 the near limbs are the ones closest to the viewer.
  The far ones are partly behind the body, but are still drawn complete.
- Both feet always point the same way the body faces in this view, never backwards and
  never sideways against the view. Toes forward, heel behind.
- Draw every leg and foot piece the same way round in all five sheets: no mirrored or
  swapped feet, no left foot in a right-foot cell.

=== JOINTS (important for animation) ===
- Each limb piece hangs STRAIGHT DOWN, centred horizontally in its cell, with its top
  joint (the point it rotates around) at the cell's top centre (x = 128, y = 30).
- Joint ends are ROUNDED and extended about 12% past the joint, like a ball joint, so the
  part can rotate without opening a gap. Shoulders, elbows, hips and knees are fully
  painted on BOTH pieces that meet there. Never cut a limb off flat.
- Pieces are complete: nothing is hidden by another part, even where the body normally
  covers it. Draw the full far arm, the full far leg, and the torso under the cape.
- The torso has NO neck stub: it ends flat at the collar. The neck belongs to the head
  piece.
- Each piece is one solid shape with no holes, except where the design itself is open.
- Armour, straps and ornaments stay on the piece they are attached to and do not hang
  across a joint onto the next piece.

=== CELL CONTENTS ===
Row 0:
  0 ASSEMBLED FIGURE in the rest pose, all parts together, weapon carried, feet on the
    cell bottom (y = 310), head near the top. This is the size reference for every
    other piece.
  1 HEAD with all its headgear, hair, horns, frill or ears, and the full neck. Its pivot
    is the base of the neck at the cell's bottom centre (x = 128, y = 300).
  2 The same HEAD with its eyes closed (blink). Otherwise identical, in the same position.
  3 TORSO: chest, armour, collar and shoulders, from the collar to the waist. No arms,
    no cape, no neck. Its waist is at the bottom centre.
  4 PELVIS: belt, hips and the skirt / kilt / trousers down to mid-thigh. No legs. Waist
    joint at the top centre.
  5 CAPE / BACK CLOTH alone ({CAPE}), hanging straight, its top edge at the top centre.
    (If "none": leave this cell empty magenta.)
  6 FRONT CLOTH alone ({FRONT CLOTH}), top edge at the top centre.
    (If "none": leave this cell empty magenta.)
  7 WEAPON AT REST: {WEAPON}. Grip at the cell centre; if it has a direction, it points
    to the RIGHT.
Row 1 (NEAR side = the character's right):
  0 UPPER ARM with its shoulder piece (shoulder to elbow). Shoulder joint at top centre.
  1 FOREARM + OPEN HAND (elbow to fingertips). Elbow at top centre.
  2 FOREARM + FIST gripping (as if holding the weapon's grip). Elbow at top centre.
  3 FOREARM + {HANDS}. Elbow at top centre.
  4 THIGH (hip to knee). Hip joint at top centre.
  5 SHIN + FOOT (knee to sole), foot flat on the ground. Knee at top centre.
  6 SHIN + FOOT on its toes (heel raised, for the walk). Knee at top centre.
  7 WEAPON ACTIVE: {WEAPON ACTIVE}. Its grip is in the same place as in row 0, cell 7.
Row 2 (FAR side = the character's left, painted slightly darker):
  0 UPPER ARM.  1 FOREARM + OPEN HAND.  2 FOREARM + FIST gripping.
  3 FOREARM + {HANDS}.  4 THIGH.  5 SHIN + FOOT flat.  6 SHIN + FOOT on its toes.
  7 WEAPON ALTERNATE: {WEAPON ALT}. (If "none": leave this cell empty magenta.)
  (Same joint rules as row 1.)

=== RULES ===
- Do not use magenta (#FF00FF), pink or purple anywhere in the artwork. Pick other
  colours for those details.
- No text, no labels, no numbers, no signature, no watermark.
- One part per cell. Never draw a part twice, never swap two parts, never put a part
  in a cell meant for another part.
- Same character, same colours and same scale as the attached sheets.

==================================================================================
PROMPT B - WEAPON EFFECTS SHEET (send once)
==================================================================================
Create a game sprite sheet of weapon effects for this character: {CHARACTER}, armed with
{WEAPON}. Effects: {EFFECTS}. Colours to match: {PALETTE}. Glowing energy cores. Match
the art style of the attached sheet.

=== CANVAS (exact) ===
- Image size: exactly 2048 x 512 pixels.
- Background: flat solid pure black #000000 everywhere that is not an effect. The effects
  are glowing light and are added on top of the game with additive blending. Their
  darkest parts fade to black, never to a grey or coloured box.
- No grid lines, no labels, no text, no frames.
- Grid: 8 columns x 2 rows of cells, each exactly 256 x 256 pixels. One effect per cell,
  centred, never crossing its cell, at least 8 px of black around it.
- Orthographic, flat 2D, no perspective.

=== CELL CONTENTS ===
Row 0 - PROJECTILES, each pointing exactly RIGHT (horizontal, tip toward x = 256),
  centred on the cell's middle row, about 200 px long or less:
  0 standard projectile, 1-5 five stronger or elemental versions of it (e.g. fire / plasma,
  piercing, shock / electric, ice / cryo, heavy / charged), 6 the standard projectile's
  trail segment alone (fading out to the left), 7 a small spark / ember particle (round,
  soft).
Row 1 - FLASHES AND IMPACTS (centred, round-ish, about 200 px wide or less):
  0 muzzle / release flash (the burst at the weapon when it fires), 1-5 one impact burst
  for each projectile in row 0 cells 1-5 (same colours), 6 charging / casting glow (a
  ring or halo), 7 smoke puff (grey, soft).

=== RULES ===
- No text, no labels, no watermark. Nothing but the effects on pure black.
- Each projectile and its impact use the same colours.

==================================================================================
CHECKLIST (check each sheet before moving on)
==================================================================================
[ ] Exactly 2048 x 960 (effects: 2048 x 512); flat magenta (effects: black) background,
    no grid lines or text.
[ ] 24 cells, one piece in each (empty only where "none"), none crossing its cell, a
    clear gap between the rows.
[ ] The pieces rebuild the assembled figure: the same scale, the head not enlarged, the
    neck short.
[ ] The torso has no neck stub; the head piece carries the neck.
[ ] Every limb hangs straight down, its joint at the top centre, with rounded ends.
[ ] Both feet point the same way as the body, and are drawn the same way round as in the
    FRONT 3/4 sheet. No backwards or swapped feet.
[ ] Near (right) limbs in row 1, far (left) limbs in row 2, the far ones slightly darker.
[ ] The weapon points right, its active version's grip is where the resting one's is.
[ ] No magenta / pink / purple inside the artwork.
[ ] The same design, colours and ornaments as the reference and the FRONT 3/4 sheet.

COMMON FIXES (send as a follow-up message with the bad sheet attached)
- Wrong size / grid: "Redraw at exactly 2048 x 960 px, 8 x 3 cells of 256 x 320 px, one
  piece per cell."
- Cropped or cut-off limb: "Draw the whole [part] with rounded joint ends; nothing hidden."
- Big head: "Draw the head at the same scale as the assembled figure, not enlarged."
- Backwards feet: "Both feet point [down-right / right / up-right], the same way the body
  faces, toes forward."
- Inconsistent character: "Keep exactly the design and colours of the attached FRONT
  3/4 sheet."
- Parts merged together: "Draw each part separately in its own cell, with magenta
  around it."
- Shadows or a floor under the figure: "No shadow, no floor: flat magenta background."
